title: Last-mile handoff notes (3rd watch)
content:
SHIFT WINDOW: 03:00-07:00 PT
OWNER: Ava Patel (third watch)
SUMMARY: Quiet night overall. Two short blips: a 4m latency spike around 03:42 affecting hosted-api route /v1/generate and an instance OOM in dedicated pool 12 at 04:20. Both recovered automatically but left a few artifacts to follow up. Leaving quick, actionable items and a trimmed mini-runbook for the next pager.

INCIDENTS (quick):
- 03:42 latency spike (hosted-api /v1/generate):
  * Symptoms: CPU on node gdn-host-07 jumped to 95%, p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 2.8s for ~4 minutes. Error rate stable (5xx not increased).
  * Immediate action taken: throttling rules temporarily tightened (route qps limit from 120 -> 80) via console to reduce tail latency; autoscaler scaled from 6 -> 8 instances; KV prefix cache warmed on new nodes.
  * Notes: spike coincided with a heavy batch of long-context streaming requests from client key kb_9X (see slack thread). No customer-facing downtime reported.
  * Follow-ups: check model-specific kernel selection logs for node gdn-host-07 (possible miscompiled kernel causing CPU soft lock). File JIRA INF-2345 assigned to @Priya.

- 04:20 OOM in dedicated pool 12 (dedicated-pool-12-node-4):
  * Symptoms: container killed with OOM, restarted and recovered, small burst of 502s for 30s.
  * Immediate action: removed a single high-memory background job (local eval runner) from that node, rebalanced load.
  * Notes: node was running quantized-mistral-70b-q4_0 with 8k context; memory spike correlated with a long pinned prefix cache build for a popular customer.
  * Follow-ups: add node-level memory soft limit and alert to avoid future hard kills. Ticket created INF-2347.

CHECKS TO RUN (if you wake to alerts):
1) Latency spike checklist (fast):
   - Open Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/latency-overview (check p50/p95/p99 across models).
   - kubectl top nodes | grep gdn-host-07 (watch CPU/mem).
   - curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-token>" https://api.redwood.test/v1/health (expect 200).
   - Tail runtime logs for route: gcloud logging read "resource.labels.instance_id=gdn-host-07 AND jsonPayload.route='/v1/generate'" --limit 200 --order asc.
   - If p99 > 5s and CPU > 90%: toggle route QPS limit to 50 and escalate to SRE pager.

2) OOM checklist (fast):
   - kubectl get pods -n dedicated-pool-12 -o wide | grep OOM
   - kubectl logs <pod> --previous | grep -i oom
   - Check node memory pressure: ssh node && free -h; dmesg | grep -i oom
   - If container keeps restarting: cordon node and spin up replacement from pool-12-template.

QUICK COMMANDS (copy/paste):
- Throttle route: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","qps":50}' https://console.redwood.test/api/route-config
- Cordon node: gcloud compute ssh operator@gdn-host-07 -- sudo kubectl cordon gdn-host-07
- Recreate node: terraform apply -target=module.dedicated_pool[12].instance_group --auto-approve

OPEN ACTIONS (to be picked up in daylight):
- INF-2345 (Priya): kernel selection logs + possible regression from last runtime build (look for mismatched AVX paths).
- INF-2347 (Ethan): implement memory soft-limits on dedicated-pool-12 nodes and add alert when RSS > 85% of host memory.
- Small doc: add a short section in runbook about long-prefix cache builds and memory accounting for quantized large-context models (this should reference optimize/recommendations).

KNOWN QUIRKS / NOTES FOR NEXT SHIFT:
- The autoscaler currently uses CPU+latency heuristics; during the latency spike CPU rose before latency dropped — consider adjusting scale-up sensitivity for streaming routes (increase lookback window).
- There is an intermittent mismatch between kernel selection logs and what the runtime reports in the metrics map; may be logging race.
- Customer kb_9X is running long streaming sessions that stress prefix caches; consider contacting solutions-eng to propose cache TTL tuning.

ESCALATION CONTACTS: (order)
1) On-call SRE: Ethan Morales (pager: +1 555-0113)
2) Backend lead (runtime): Priya Singh (slack: @priyas, phone: +1 555-0177)
3) Duty manager: Sarah Ko (slack: @sarahk)

HANDOFF BULLETS (for next):
- Check INF-2345 & INF-2347 status before shift end.
- Watch for more alerts on route /v1/generate and dedicated-pool-12.
- If additional latency spikes, consider immediate model fallback to 'mistral-7b-v2' for non-critical traffic (console toggle exists under Hosted -> Routing -> Fallbacks).
- No customer escalations open right now. No on-call postmortem expected unless incidents reoccur.

LIGHTHOUSE TASKS (low-effort follow-ups):
- Add a short cron job to rotate local eval runners off nodes during peak hours. (15–30m to implement)
- Draft a short note to solutions-eng re: long prefix sessions.

NOTES TO SELF:
- Remember to attach screenshots of the Grafana spike to INF-2345.
- Save a sample of kernel selection trace: /var/log/runtime/kernel-select.log.

END OF NOTE — thanks, next person.

Signature: Ava P.
